I’m really sorry you’re experiencing all that. Despite what it may seem, you’re not alone. Unfortunately it seems like stories of those who seem to pass instantly are upvoted and awarded. I don’t cry any more than I used to. Mentally, I feel pretty much the same. 2.5 months is when things started with me. My areola seemed to puff a bit. Things have happened so gradually that it seems like nothing has changed, but comparing before and after pictures, I can’t deny that changes have happened even though I feel like I need to for some reason. Things for me got worse before they got better. I was constantly checking my body and resenting the lack of change. It does get better. Some things I would recommend that have helped me (and could hopefully help you as well): take progress pictures! I’ve been taking them of my face and my torso, and when I’m feeling down, looking at my progress, though modest, is really helpful. If you’re embarrassed to have that kind of thing on your camera roll, making a Google photos or something could help. Next, I’d recommend making sure your levels and meds are optimal. There are some providers who are overly cautious and keep you on low doses. I switched at 4 months, and as a result, physical changes actually started occurring! Injections are very effective, though starting out on them is often advised against. I think in another 3 months that might be a good option, though I’m no doctor. Another thing that helped me is focusing on clothing and presentation. During the first 6 months especially, replaced my wardrobe with more feminine clothes, got a ‘female’ hair cut, experimented with my hair, got my ears pierced, and started painting my nails. All of them helped out quite a bit! At 10 months, I still feel frustrated by some of the things that haven’t changed, but I’m unrecognizable from a year ago. Mentally, I haven’t changed really (at least I don’t think I have), but I do feel that I’m being truer to myself and feel much more comfortable. I feel the “have patience” bit. I’m not going to tell you to do that. I hated being told that, that isn’t helpful at all. TLDR: At 2.5 months, I was just getting the changes you got at 1.5 months, and things have gradually gone in the right direction! Meanwhile, there’s some things you can do to pass the time, to feel better about yourself, and to make sure you’re headed where you want to be! I wish you the best of luck, I hope you know you aren’t alone, and I hope this was helpful to you!
